text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The Polish President's Office has spent 6.0 million zlotys on a campaign promoting the new constitution to be voted on in a referendum on Sunday. The Office financed direct mailing of copies of the constitution to 12 million households.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
- The cabinet's socio-economic strategy council has given preliminary approval to the social security reform programme produced by the government.

- Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), the state-owned telecoms monopolist, said it launched a new Inmarsat Mini M service for digital telephone and fax transmission, as well as access to the public telephone network and inter-terminal connections.

- The Polish Capital Group (PGK) including major Polish investors interested in buying 75 percent of the Ruch press distribution chain slated for privatisation has complained about the inadequacy of documents provided by the treasury ministry which makes it hard to present a well-prepared price offer, PGK said.
- Poles bought 43,800 new cars in April, showing a 29.4 percent growth compared with the same period last year, the Samar car market monitoring firm said.

- The Winiary food concentrate maker, controlled by Nestle, will spend all of its 1996 net profit reaching 5.1 million zlotys on plant development and modernisation, Winiary's president Karol Madrowski said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- Poland's inflation rate will fall to 13 percent by the end of 1997, Finance Minister Marek Belka said.

- Poland's industrial output is likely to grow by 8.5 percent in 1997 compared with last year and construction output will go up by 13 percent, a report by the cabinet's strategic studies centre (RCSS) said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The Elseter electrical engineering firm, controlled by the listed Elektrim foreign trade group, plans to develop co-operation with the US General Electric (GE), Elseter's president Wieslaw Adam Brzozowski said. GE is considering a joint venture with Elseter to build a low voltage equipment plant.
ZYCIE

- Poles bought 144,224 new cars in the first four months of 1997 showing a 30 percent growth compared with the same period last year, Samar said. Fiat sold 60,742 cars in the period, followed by Daewoo with sales of 40,134 cars.
- JTT Computer, Poland's second biggest computer firm, will soon present computer system offers to the government and Telekomunikacja Polska SA, JTT Computer said.
PARKIET
- The Warsaw Stock Exchange board has permitted bourse listing of the shares of Bank Handlowy which is now undergoing privatisation.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
